extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP practitioners, applicants and in-house counsel working in Mexico and Ecuador
extracted.subtask_description: Country-specific guidance for prosecuting and enforcing industrial property rights (patents and related IP) in Mexico and Ecuador, covering patentability standards, claim-drafting, prosecution formalities (PCT/Paris/PPH), divisional practice, enforcement procedures, remedies, invalidity grounds, timelines and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain name registration prohibition (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organic Code for the Social Knowledge and Innovation Economy of Ecuador prohibits registration, trafficking in, or use of a domain name that is identical or confusingly similar to, or dilutive of, another person’s mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of trademark infringement (Ecuador) — enumerated acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration confers the right to act against third parties who, without consent, perform acts in relation to identical or similar products/services including: (a) using or affixing the mark on products/containers/packaging; (b) deleting or modifying the mark for commercial purposes; (c) manufacturing labels/packaging that reproduce the trademark and selling/storing such materials; (d) use in trade of identical/similar sign that may cause confusion or economic/commercial damage; (e) use in trade of identical/similar sign to a well-known trademark causing dilution or unfair advantage; (f) public use of identical/similar well-known mark where it could cause dilution even for non-commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is presumed there is a possibility of confusion when dealing with an identical sign to distinguish identical products or services. The titleholder may impede listed acts irrespective of whether they are carried out via digital communication networks or other channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural options for trademark enforcement (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark owners have administrative and jurisdictional (court) actions available; administrative protection of industrial property rights is the most effective way to enforce rights in Ecuador.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing for trademark actions (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal standing is limited to any person who has a legitimate interest, either as a consumer or as a trademark titleholder. If the trademark holder has not yet filed an infringement action, a potential infringer may request a negative enforcement action to declare that its conduct does not infringe the trademark rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court system for trademark enforcement (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage enforcement: Administrative Stage (National Director of Industrial Property, appeal to Intellectual Property Committee) and Jurisdictional Stage (judge of place where defendant is located or where infringement has effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a high level of expertise at the Administrative Stage and a medium-low level at the Jurisdictional Stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation delay (Ecuador trademark administrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time to reach a first instance decision in an administrative stage is 1 to 2 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations for infringement (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Article 244 of Decision 486, time limit for seeking a remedy for patent (IP) infringement is 2 years counted from the date the patent holder had knowledge of the infringement, or in any case 5 years counted from the date the last act of infringement occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction grounds (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary injunctions available when (1) the complaint contains proof on specific and consistent evidence reasonably presuming actual or imminent violation; or (2) when inspections prove, even presumptively, violation of an IP right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary injunctions may be confirmed or revoked in the final resolution. Ex-parte remedies are described as the most effective and efficient ways to stop infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctive relief measures (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible injunctive relief includes: ceasing violation acts; withdrawal from commercial channels of infringing products (including packaging and advertising materials); suspension of public communication of protected content in digital media ordered against offender or intermediary; suspension of web portal services; suspension of import/export of goods/materials (notified to customs); temporary closure of alleged offender's establishment when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bifurcated procedure for infringement vs invalidity (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: An infringement process may take place before the National Direction of Industrial Property while an invalidity process may take place before the Committee of Intellectual Property (procedures may be bifurcated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark invalidity grounds (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration to nullify a registration can be filed in cases: (a) registry granted on basis of false data/documents essential for concession; (b) registry not intrinsically distinctive; (c) registry not extrinsically distinctive; (d) registry obtained in bad faith (examples provided, e.g., representative obtaining foreign mark registration without consent; habitual activity of registering trademarks for commercialization); (e) registry obtained in violation of procedure or law that substantially influenced grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-trial discovery procedures (Ecuador trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organic Code provides pre-trial discovery and procedures to preserve evidence of infringement or identify the infringer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary support — burden of proof & experts (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must present evidentiary support; expert witnesses may provide reports based on questions or requests made by parties to help judges resolve the case. Parties may present witnesses and the court may appoint its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages for trademark infringement (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain damages from the losing party you must initiate an independent civil action (separate from administrative enforcement).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADR & settlement (Ecuador)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arbitration in IP is not available in Ecuador; however parties can mediate to settle the case outside the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal liability and sanctions (Ecuador trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is personal liability in criminal infringement actions. Sanctions for criminal actions are only criminal fines; no prison is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant patent regulations and treaties (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent practice governed by Industrial Property Law, its regulations, Paris Convention, PCT, and PPH agreements with various offices (EPO, USPTO, JPO, CNIPA, KIPO, IPOS, and Pacific Alliance offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions that are new, involve an inventive step and are capable of industrial application are patentable. Utility models and designs are protected via registrations (not patents). Computer programs are not considered inventions but computer-implemented processes may be patentable. Certain categories (essentially biological processes to obtain/propagate plants/animals; mental processes/games/business methods/mathematical methods; methods of presenting information; methods of surgical/therapeutic/diagnostic treatment) are excluded or treated with restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therapeutic treatment methods may be claimed using Swiss-type or purpose-limited product claims; IMPI practice varies and it is recommended to file purpose-limited product claim format where possible. Ex vivo diagnostic methods may be allowed in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush claims and biological deposits (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Markush claims are patentable if duly supported in the specification and meet patentability requirements. Mexico accepts deposits of a wide range of microorganisms/materials under recognized IDAs (Budapest Treaty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkage system (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Linkage regulation requires IMPI to publish a gazette listing patents in force that cover allopathic medicines every six months; COFEPRIS must observe listed patents when granting marketing authorizations. Certain patents (manufacture/formulation processes) excluded; inclusion of formulation patents in linkage gazette acts as a preventive measure to avoid grant of marketing approvals that would infringe patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMPI historically interpreted linkage narrowly; litigation has included some 'use' patents notwithstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art / novelty determination (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: State of the art on the filing date (or recognized priority date) is used to determine novelty and inventive step. State of the art includes all patent applications filed in Mexico prior to that date and still pending, even if publication occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure by the inventor within 12 months prior to filing (e.g., national/international exhibition, public disclosure, or putting into practice) shall not prevent novelty in certain circumstances — evidentiary documents required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inventive step (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Inventive step" means the creative process the results of which are not obviously deductible from the state of the art by a person skilled in the relevant art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim clarity and drafting recommendations (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be clear, concise and not extend beyond contents of the specification. Claims should be drafted according to the technical features of the invention. The first claim must be independent and relate to the essential feature; independent claims should, if possible, include a preamble (features already in prior art) and a characterizing part (novel subject matter). Further technical features should be pursued via dependent claims, ensuring consistent dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and process claim scope and exclusions (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and process claims are patentable if they meet patentability requirements except for: (i) essentially biological processes for plants/animals; (ii) methods that are mental processes, playing games, doing business, mathematical methods; (iii) methods of presenting information; (iv) methods of surgical, therapeutic or diagnostic treatment applicable to humans/animals (subject to claim formulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therapeutic methods may be claimed as Swiss-type or purpose-limited product claims; IMPI practice varies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT application formalities (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements when entering national phase/PCT: copy of International application as published (specification, claims, abstract, PCT publication sheet); formal drawings (translate legends to Spanish); copy of amendments during international phase; assignment of rights not required; power of attorney on behalf of applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paris Convention regular application formalities (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required: copy of specification, claims and abstract; formal drawings (if any); certified copy of priority right document; data sheet with inventors' and applicants' details and priority info; assignment of rights; power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH program participation requirements (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: To request PPH participation, provide: copies of all relevant Office actions from foreign office showing allowable/patentable claims (with Spanish translations); copies of patentable claims determined by USPTO (with Spanish translation); an IDS listing documents cited by USPTO and copies of cited documents (including non-patent literature) unless available to IMPI; ensure MX examination has not begun and MX publication has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications are not published in Mexico — watch timing; IMPI may retrieve some foreign documents from public PAIR, but applicants should submit missing copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME and institutional fee discounts (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPI applies a 50% fee discount on fees to universities, independent inventors, educational institutions, research institutions and small and medium entities filing an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition / third-party observations (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: No opposition system per se. Within six months after publication a third party may file information related to patentability for IMPI's consideration at the examiner's discretion; such filers are not parties, do not have access to the application file, and have no immediate legal standing to challenge a granted patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interviews (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners are not expressly regulated by law but examiners are usually willing to hear applicants. Such interviews are not binding on examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection provided by pending applications (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights are enforceable after granting of the patent; pending applications do not provide enforceable patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and extensions (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent term is 20 years from the filing date. No term extensions are available in Mexico.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications are not allowed in Mexico.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can request expedited examination of patent applications in Mexico by using PPH provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendments after grant (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text or drawings of a granted patent may only be amended by the patent owner to (i) correct obvious/form errors; and (ii) limit the scope of the claims. Authorized changes shall be published in the Official Gazette. An amendment after allowance is requested in writing with brief reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional practice and unity (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: If application fails unity of invention, applicant must divide and file divisional(s) simultaneously with the response to that requirement; non-elected claims should be filed as divisional application(s). Practice accepts voluntary divisional applications before payment of final fees and prior to substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of patent infringement (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement generally occurs when a third unauthorized party makes, uses or sells a patented product or process. The test of infringement is whether the patent claims would cover the accused product or process via claim construction (legal) and claim coverage (factual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement can only be literal under IP Law; doctrine of equivalents not recognized. For process claims where the patent is for a process obtaining a product, the defendant bears burden to show product was made by another process if product is new or there is substantial likelihood the accused product was made by the patented process and patentee cannot determine the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributory infringement and multiple infringers (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: The law does not recognize theory of contributory infringement; only direct infringers (those making/using/selling) can be liable. Multiple direct infringers can be held equally liable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization, licenses and implied rights (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization to make/use/sell is principally through a license. Implied licenses may arise (e.g., buyer of a patented product may have right to repair and resell). Compulsory licenses exist in law but are difficult to obtain and have not been granted in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territoriality of infringement (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement is produced when committed within the territory of the Republic of Mexico. Exception: use in a foreign vessel, aircraft or vehicle in transit in Mexico is not considered infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMPI administrative infringement procedure (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPI handles infringement in first instance via administrative proceedings: plaintiff files a formal written claim; IMPI admits the claim and serves notice to defendant who has 10 days to answer; both parties must produce supporting evidence at filing/answer; IMPI decides on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMPI is an administrative agency, not a court of law. Criminal sanctions may apply for recidivism through PGR (Federal District Attorney Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal sanctions for patent infringement (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal actions for patent infringement are available only for re-offense cases (recidivism), where a party infringes after a final decision from IMPI declaring infringement. Such re-offense can be punished with up to 6 years imprisonment and a fine, and may be pursued ex-officio or ex-parte through PGR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to sue and counterclaims (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patentee or licensee (unless expressly forbidden) has right to prosecute an infringement suit. A distributor may not bring a suit. An accused infringer may counterclaim patent invalidity under formal or technical considerations when responding to an IMPI infringement suit. Amendments allow anyone to request IMPI to officiously initiate cancellation proceedings against patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple legal standing (mere business/commercial activity) to challenge patent validity is under judicial test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial expertise and appellate structure (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPI handles first instance administrative patent enforcement. A specialized IP Court at the Federal Court for Administrative Affairs (since Jan 2009) reviews cases under the IP Law; last appeal stage is Federal Circuit Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMPI is considered the only authority for first instance patent enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation delay and timeline (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial stage before IMPI for a patent infringement action usually takes 18 to 20 months. Two further stages of appeals before courts may last no less than three further years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations and damages timing (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no general statute of limitations stated, however there is a two-year limitation period to pursue a civil action for damages; thus timing affects damages claims. Monetary relief available in civil actions typically consists of actual losses and lost profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunctions and interim reliefs (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPI may order alleged infringer to stop infringing activities, withdraw products from marketplace and conduct seizures. Proceedings for interim relief are inaudita altera pars (without formal hearing); the patentee must file an infringement claim within twenty business days after measures are notified. Preliminary injunctions may be confirmed and become permanent only once infringement action resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff does not have to show likelihood of success to obtain injunctions; marking is a condition to request a preliminary injunction and to the awarding of monetary damages (marking can be substituted by nationwide publication claiming ownership). Plaintiff must post a reasonable bond; defendant can lift measures by placing a counter bond equal to plaintiff's plus 40%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-parte remedies (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain remedies (including seizures and preliminary measures) can be issued ex parte; criminal remedies available only for re-offense cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are often effective but require timely follow-up infringement claims and bonds as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds practice (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff is required to post a bond of a reasonable amount to warrant possible damages to defendant to obtain preliminary injunctions. Defendant may post a counter-bond (same amount plus 40%) to lift measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no fixed guidelines established for bond amounts; practice varies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil remedies for patent infringement (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies available through civil actions (filed after administrative action resolved) include monetary relief in the form of actual losses and lost profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity / revocation procedures and grounds (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity (revocation) can be raised as a counterclaim in response to an infringement action or as an independent action. Grounds include: (1) patent granted in contravention of requirements/conditions for grant; (2) patent granted in contravention of law in force at the time of granting; (3) patent application was abandoned while prosecuted; (4) patent granted by error or to someone not entitled. Causes (1) and (2) may be filed at any time; causes (3) and (4) must be filed within five years from the patent's publication effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An independent invalidity action not filed together with the infringement response will be decided separately from the infringement case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery and pre-trial procedures (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery/pre-trial procedures exist to preserve evidence or identify the infringer; in administrative infringement proceedings parties must produce supporting evidence at the time of filing/answering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence, experts and witnesses (Mexico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must produce supporting evidence when filing/answering; expert evidence and witness testimony are used to assist adjudicators. Expert reports are prepared based on requests/questions from parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and fees (Ecuador/Mexico) — illustrative figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Average professional fees for a first instance decision (Ecuador trademark example) may be between US$4,000.00 to US$7,000.00. IMPI applies fee discounts for eligible entities (Mexico).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual costs vary by case complexity and counsel.
